question: A resident says water crossed the eastern yard during heavy rain. The learner visited on a dry day. How should the note be labelled?

choices.label: A measured flood level
choices.feedback: No flood level was measured. Keep the resident’s account and identify what still needs checking.

choices.label: Reported experience
choices.feedback: Yes. The resident’s experience is useful evidence, and its source stays visible. It is not a measured contour or flood depth.

choices.label: A proposal to dig a drain
choices.feedback: The account describes what a resident experienced. A drain would be a separate proposal needing site assessment and relevant checks.

question: The sketch says “not to scale”. A new rectangle fits beside the drawn path. What can the learner conclude?

choices.label: The new bed will fit on the ground
choices.feedback: Its appearance on an unscaled sketch cannot establish fit. Relevant measurements and the system’s requirements are still needed.

choices.label: Exporting the sketch will verify its dimensions
choices.feedback: An export preserves a view; it does not add missing measurements or verify a boundary.

choices.label: It is an idea to check against measurements
choices.feedback: Yes. Keep the idea on a proposal overlay and obtain the measurements needed before claiming it fits.

question: The household does not want animals in this first phase. Their care capacity is not yet recorded. What should the design do?

choices.label: Keep animals outside this phase and follow the agreed brief
choices.feedback: Yes. A design does not need every possible system. Follow the household’s priorities and confirm care for what is proposed.

choices.label: Add chickens because every permaculture plan needs them
choices.feedback: The household has not agreed to that system. A design is judged by how it meets the brief, not by including a standard list of animals.

choices.label: Assign animal care to whoever usually carries water
choices.feedback: Existing work is not consent to additional work. Care responsibilities need discussion and agreement.
